title: `sort` is stable on the probe, guaranteed only with `maintain_order`
description: Sorting 200 000 rows on a key with 7 values kept the input order within each key, in memory and streaming, with and without `maintain_order`. Polars documents order among ties only for `maintain_order=True`.
`top_k` keeps 2 of 3 tied rows; which ones is not documented.
reference: `tie_order`: any order of the ties, and any rows of a tie for a `fetch`. Every behaviour is allowed.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
